title: GhJSON
description: A Grasshopper definition serialised as GhJSON, ready to be placed directly onto the canvas. Output exactly this structure — no prose, no markdown fences, no explanation. Only the raw JSON object.
rules: name must exactly match the component's name in the Grasshopper library (case-sensitive), e.g. 'Addition', 'Construct Point', 'Number Slider'.

Use only native Grasshopper components. Do NOT use any scripting components (Python 3 Script, C# Script, GhPython, VB Script, or any other code-bearing node) — code generation is handled by a separate tool, and a script component placed here is an error.
Every component needs a unique integer id. Connections and any references use this id.
instanceGuid is optional and may be omitted: components are placed with regenerated instance GUIDs, so any value you supply is discarded. Do not spend effort inventing UUIDs.

Every component needs a pivot 'X,Y' giving its canvas position. There is no automatic layout pass — you set the positions. Lay the graph out left to right following data flow: source components (sliders, params) on the far left, results on the right. Use about 150 units between pipeline stages (X) and about 80 units between parallel inputs feeding the same component (Y).

connections has one entry per wired input. A component with three wired inputs (e.g. Construct Point X, Y, Z) needs three separate connection entries pointing to it. Reference each endpoint by { id, paramIndex }: id selects the component, and paramIndex is the parameter's zero-based position in that component's list — the OUTPUT list for the wire's 'from', the INPUT list for its 'to' — counting in the order shown in componentCatalog (first parameter = 0). paramName is optional and for readability only; the wire is matched by paramIndex.

Do not leave a non-source component's inputs all unwired. Any downstream component that should receive data but has no incoming connections is reported as a placement failure. Source components (Number Slider, Panel acting as input, Boolean Toggle, value params) legitimately have no inputs.
Number Slider value uses the format 'default<min~max>', e.g. '5<0~10>', set at componentState.extensions['gh.numberslider'].value. This is the most common mistake — do not use a plain number.

Give every Number Slider (and other input source, e.g. Boolean Toggle, Value List) a nickName naming what it controls — 'Radius', 'Height', 'Point Count' — so the definition reads clearly on the canvas. Never leave a slider with its default 'Number Slider' label. Short and specific; optional on other components.

To reuse an input already on the canvas (listed in the grounding as 'inputs already on the canvas', e.g. 'baseCurve (Curve)'), add a parameter node of that geometry type ('Curve' or 'Point') whose nickName is the input's EXACT name, give it no incoming connection, and wire from its output — it is spliced onto the existing Rhino object instead of being created. Only names the grounding lists resolve this way; never invent one, and never build a fresh param for geometry that already exists.
Colours use the prefixed string 'argb:A,R,G,B' where each channel is 0-255, e.g. 'argb:255,200,220,240'.

Component-type-specific values (slider range, panel text, value-list items, etc.) live under componentState.extensions, keyed by the extension name (e.g. 'gh.numberslider', 'gh.panel'). Standard components with no special state omit componentState entirely.
Omit document metadata and groups — they are not needed and are not part of this schema. Output only the raw JSON object.

componentCatalog.description: Parameters for common Grasshopper components, listed in order. A parameter's paramIndex is its zero-based position in the inputs or outputs array below (first = 0); use that as the paramIndex in connections, and the label as the optional paramName. Components with no inputs are data sources and need no incoming connections.

components.description: All Grasshopper components in the definition.

connections.description: Wires between component parameters. One entry per wire — a component with N wired inputs needs N entries, one per input parameter.

name.description: Component display name, exactly as it appears in the Grasshopper library, e.g. 'Addition', 'Number Slider', 'Sphere'.

id.description: Unique integer identifier, referenced by the connections array.

instanceGuid.description: Optional UUID v4. Regenerated on placement, so it may be omitted.

componentGuid.description: Optional component-type GUID. Leave this out — it is filled in by Physalia's component resolver from the live library. Do not invent a value; an incorrect GUID prevents the component from being created.

nickName.description: On-canvas label for the component. Set it on every input source — most importantly a Number Slider — to name what it controls (e.g. 'Radius', 'Height'); short and specific. Optional for other components.

inputSettings.description: Optional per-input parameter settings. Only needed to change a parameter's behaviour (data mapping, reversed, etc.); omit otherwise.

outputSettings.description: Optional per-output parameter settings. Omit unless changing an output's behaviour.

pivot.description: Canvas position as 'X,Y' (numbers may be negative or decimal), e.g. '100,200'. Lay components out left to right following data flow.

componentState.description: Optional UI state and component-type-specific values. Omit for standard components that need no special state.

selected.description: Whether the component is selected on the canvas.

hidden.description: Whether the component's preview is hidden.

extensions.description: Component-type-specific values, keyed by extension name. Use only the key that matches the component (e.g. a Number Slider uses 'gh.numberslider').

ext_numberslider.description: Number Slider state. Used on a component whose name is 'Number Slider'.

value.description: Slider value as 'default<min~max>'. The default sits between min and max. Decimal places in the numbers set the slider's precision.

ext_panel.description: Panel state. Used on a component whose name is 'Panel'. A Panel with no input wire shows its own static 'text'; a Panel wired from upstream displays that data.

multiline.description: Whether text wraps onto multiple lines.

wrap.description: Whether text wraps within the panel width.

ext_valuelist.description: Value List state. Used on a component whose name is 'Value List'.

ext_toggle.description: Boolean Toggle state. Used on a component whose name is 'Boolean Toggle'.

ext_button.description: Button state. Used on a Button component.

corners.description: Exactly three corner offsets 'x,y' relative to the pivot: [A, B, D]. The fourth corner is derived as B + D - A.

parameterSettings.description: Settings for a single input or output parameter. Only include the fields you need to change.

expression.description: Expression that transforms the parameter's data.

connection.description: A single wire from a source output to a target input.

connectionEndpoint.description: One end of a wire. 'id' selects the component; 'paramIndex' selects the parameter.

paramIndex.description: Zero-based position of the parameter within the component's list — its OUTPUT list for the wire's 'from', its INPUT list for its 'to' — using the order shown in componentCatalog. This is how the wire is matched; always include it.

paramName.description: Optional human-readable parameter label from componentCatalog (e.g. 'A', 'Radius'). For readability only; matching uses paramIndex.
